good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/ treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Section III Exclusions > 2. Speciﬁed disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02
good.explanation: Specific illnesses are excluded for 24 months from the start of coverage. This 24-month waiting period is standard and acceptable in the market.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with insurer
good.reference: Section III Exclusions > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl 01
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 36 months from policy inception. This 36-month waiting period is common and meets market standards.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section III Exclusions > 3. 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days except accidents. A 30-day initial waiting period is standard practice.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 30 days prior to the date of hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 30 days before hospitalization are covered. This duration is typical in health insurance policies.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post Hospitalization: Medical expenses incurred for a period up to 60 days from the date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days after hospital discharge are covered. This is a standard post-hospitalization coverage period.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room, Boarding, Nursing Expenses all inclusive as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home up to 1% of the sum insured per day
bad.explanation: Room rent is capped at 1% of the sum insured per day. Such daily caps can reduce claim amounts if you choose higher category rooms.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Expenses relating to hospitalization will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent stated in the policy or actual whichever is less
bad.reference: Section II Coverage > Section I (after F)
bad.explanation: Because room rent is capped, related hospital expenses may be proportionately reduced, increasing your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatments: The expenses payable during the entire policy period for the following treatment/procedure... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below; * Sublimit all inclusive
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered but with strict sub-limits, which may lead to significant out-of-pocket expenses.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Expenses incurred on treatment of Cataract is subject to the limit as per the following table;
bad.reference: Section II Coverage > Section I (Cataract table)
bad.explanation: Cataract treatment costs are capped per eye per policy period, limiting your claim amount for this condition.

bad.name: Ambulance Cover
bad.quote: Emergency ambulance charges up-to a sum of Rs.750/- per hospitalization and overall limit of Rs.1,500/- per policy period
bad.explanation: Ambulance coverage exists but is very low compared to actual ambulance costs, potentially causing out-of-pocket expenses.

bad.name: Implants Limit
bad.quote: With regard to coronary stenting, the Company will pay such amount up to the extent of cost of bare metal stent/drug eluting cobalt-chromium stent/drug eluting stainless steel stent.
bad.explanation: Reimbursement for coronary stents is limited to specified types and costs, so higher-cost stents may not be fully covered.

bad.name: Medicines Limit
bad.quote: In respect of medicines, Implants and such other similar items, the Company will pay up to the cost of alternate indigenous make
bad.explanation: Reimbursement for medicines and implants is limited to the cost of indigenous alternatives, which may cause extra expense if imported brands are used.

bad.name: Co-pay

bad.explanation: A 20% co-pay applies for entry age 61 and above. Any co-pay clause makes the policy less favorable as it increases your out-of-pocket costs.
